title: ATOMS: ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-forming regions - X. Chemical differentiation among the massive cores in G9.62+0.19
question: Investigate the physical and chemical conditions (rotational temperatures, column densities, abundances, chemical differentiation, and COM formation routes) of dense cores at different evolutionary stages in G9.62+0.19.

data.sensitivity: 12-m continuum: 0.4 mJy beam^-1; 12-m+ACA continuum: ~0.5 mJy beam^-1; 12-m SPWs 1-4: 8 mJy beam^-1 ch^-1, SPWs 5-6: 10 mJy beam^-1 ch^-1, SPWs 7-8: 3 mJy beam^-1 ch^-1; combined SiO/HCO+/CS: ~13, 60, 48 mJy beam^-1 ch^-1

what.value: ALMA 1.3 mm continuum data of G9.62+0.19 used to derive H2 column densities

evidence.quote: Instead, we use 1.3 mm continuum data from (cite: Liu17), and smooth it to the same spatial resolution as that of 3 mm continuum data.

what.value: Volume densities of starless cores MM2, MM3, MM5, MM9, MM10, and MM12

evidence.loc: Results / Molecular lines identification / Molecular lines from different cores
evidence.quote: It is worth to mention that MM3 and MM9 have larger volume density (6.1$\times$10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$ and 15.9$\times$10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$) than other four starless cores (1.9$\times$10$^{6}$, 2.2$\times$10$^{6}$, 2.8$\times$10$^{6}$, and 0.6$\times$10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$ for MM2, MM5, MM10, and MM12, respectively; see more details in Table 1 of (cite: Liu17)).

what.value: Molecular abundances relative to CH3OH and H2 in HMSFRs, LMSFRs, and GCMCs (Table 4)

evidence.loc: Discussions / Physical parameters of individual molecule
evidence.quote: We also compare molecular abundances with respect to H$_{2}$ and CH$_{3}$OH derived in our work with those derived in other sources including high-mass star forming regions (HMSFRs), low-mass star forming regions (LMSFRs) and Galactic Center molecular clouds (GCMCs).

recipe.method: Two-dimensional Gaussian fitting to the 12-m array and 12-m+ACA combined 3 mm continuum maps to obtain positions, sizes, peak flux densities, and total flux densities of the dense cores.

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and identify molecular line transitions
recipe.method: Extract full-band beam-averaged spectra at the continuum peaks from 12-m array observations and identify transitions above 3 sigma using XCLASS with CDMS and JPL databases, requiring consistent rest frequencies, LSR velocities, and spatial distributions.
key_parameters: Detection threshold: > 3 sigma (1 sigma RMS = 0.12 - 0.14 K computed in line-free channels)
assumptions: Transitions of a specific species are excited by similar conditions and share similar LSR velocity and spatial distribution

recipe.goal: Map spatial distributions of molecular emission and outflows
recipe.method: Generate integrated intensity maps of main transitions of O-, N-, and S-bearing species and outflow tracers (SiO, HCO+, CS).

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperatures, column densities, and line optical depths via LTE spectral modeling
recipe.method: Model observed 12-m spectra using myXCLASS and MAGIX under LTE assumptions, fitting unblended transitions (>3 transitions with wide Eu range) for T_rot and N_T, or fixing T_rot to core average gas temperature when fewer than 3 transitions are detected.
key_parameters: Model parameters: source size, rotational temperature, column density, FWHM line width, velocity offset
Fixed T_rot for species with <3 transitions: 99 K (MM7), 134 K (MM8), 137 K (MM4), 100 K (MM11)
assumptions: Beam filling factor ~ 1 (very large source size) for extended components; 2D Gaussian fit to line images for compact components; free parameter when comparable to beam size

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities, molecular fractional abundances, and carbon isotopic ratios
recipe.method: Smooth archival 1.3 mm continuum data to 3 mm resolution, fit 2D Gaussians to get core sizes and fluxes, compute H2 column density and continuum optical depth, and calculate fractional abundances chi = N_T / N_H2 and 12C/13C ratios.
key_parameters: Mean molecular mass per H2 molecule mu = 2.8
Dust absorption coefficient kappa_nu = 0.899 cm^2 g^-1 at 1.3 mm
assumptions: Dust temperature equals average rotational temperature of COMs (thermal coupling at n_H2 > 10^6 cm^-3): 99 K (MM7), 134 K (MM8), 137 K (MM4), 100 K (MM11)
Dust grains with thin ice mantles at a gas density of 10^6 cm^-3
